correctness.rationale: On the high-probability event of isolated vertices on both sides, no K2,3/K3,2, and vertex-disjoint four-cycles, every non-boundary concept is either a star, a single isolated edge, or a 2×2 four-cycle biclique. A degree-two vertex on a four-cycle creates a duplicate star that is not maximal. Consequently C=2+D+I+Σ_H(1-z(H)), with z exactly the number of degree-two cycle vertices. Expected counts of forbidden K2,3 and intersecting C4 are O(1/n); independent isolation indicators force boundary concepts. Method of factorial moments yields independent Poisson C4 types with mean (c^4/4) C(4,z)e^{-cz}(1-e^{-c})^{4-z}. Disjoint cycle cross-edges affect marks with o(1) probability. The displayed characteristic function follows. Degree≥2 and isolated-edge component counts have O(n) variance and their expectations give g(c) after division by n. All signs of the integer-valued residual are retained.

originality.rationale: Concepts as maximal bicliques and formulae for expected concept counts are classical. Kovács 2018 studies an efficient approximation to expected concept number in independently sampled attributes; Sakurai 2021 derives expectation formula and an expected superpolynomial lower bound for constant-density random contexts. Neither inspected primary paper proves the sparse n×n, p=c/n law with an exact degree-statistic subtraction and a marked compound-Poisson residual. The correction is stronger than a first-moment count and not a formal consequence of previous expectation identities without sparse subgraph theory. Best of knowledge with normal bibliographic incompleteness.
residual_risks: An unindexed probabilistic maximal-biclique or random formal-context theorem could subsume the same Poisson-marked defect.
No convergence of expectations for the centered correction, no CLT for full C_n, no statement beyond fixed c and balanced sides.

value.rationale: The concept lattice is a natural object in FCA and the sparse c/n regime is a canonical random graph limit. A linear law for total concepts is useful, but the genuinely discrete marked C4 defect quantifies exactly how local biclique overlap changes the count after subtracting directly observable degree statistics. The marks include negative contributions: simply counting cycles would be wrong. This is a motivated structural-plus-distributional correction, not a routine restatement of expected-count formulas or finite table recomputation.

limitations: The deterministic identity holds only on a specified typical class; overlapping 4-cycles or K2,3 can invalidate it.
The finite Galois experiment does not establish distributional convergence or independence of marks.
